# New renderings — iliad-079 (13.169–265)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| πολυΐππου (Μέντορος, 13.171) | "rich in horses" | "who was rich in horses" | "horse-keeping", "of many horses", "horse-breeding"; πολύς "much" + ἵππος "horse", and ἱπποδάμων stays "tamer of horses" |
| κούρην … νόθην ἔχε (13.173) | "had a daughter of Priam, illegitimate" | "had for wife Priam’s illegitimate daughter" | "bastard"; νόθος keeps the table’s "illegitimate"; ἔχω of a woman is "have as wife" and the note says so |
| ἀμφιέλισσαι (νέες, 13.174) | "both-sides-curving" | "curved on both sides" | reused from the table (6.264), no departure; note says sense disputed |
| ἶσα τέκεσσι (τίεν, 13.176) | "equally with his children" | "equally with his children" | follows the table’s ἶσα φίλοισι τέκεσσι (5.71) |
| ἥ τ’ ὄρεος κορυφῇ ἕκαθεν περιφαινομένοιο (13.179, ash-tree simile) | "on the peak of a mountain seen from afar on every side" | "on the peak of a mountain seen clearly from afar" | "that shows itself all round", "visible"; περιφαίνομαι is "show oneself round about", ἕκαθεν "from afar" |
| τέρενα … φύλλα πελάσσῃ (13.180) | "brings near to the ground its tender leaves" | "lays its tender leaves down to the ground" | "bows", "sheds"; πελάζω is "bring near"; τέρην keeps the Odyssey’s "tender" |
| ἀλλ’ ὃ μὲν ἄντα ἰδὼν ἠλεύατο … τυτθόν (13.184–185) | "looking straight at it, avoided … by a little" | "seeing it coming straight at him, avoided … though only just" | "a hair’s breadth", "by a whisker"; τυτθόν is "a little" |
| Ἀκτορίων (Κτεάτου υἷ’ Ἀκτορίωνος, 13.185) | "of Actor’s line" | "of Actor’s line" | follows the table’s Ἀκτορίωνε (2.621) |
| κόρυθα κροτάφοις ἀραρυῖαν (13.188) | "the helmet fitted to the temples" | "the helmet, fitted to the temples" | "close-fitting", "tight on the brows"; κρόταφος "temple" |
| πᾶς … χαλκῷ σμερδαλέῳ κεκάλυφθ’ (13.191–192) | "all of him with frightful bronze was covered" | "covered all over with frightful bronze" | σμερδαλέος "frightful" as in the table (12.464) |
| οὔ πῃ χροὸς εἴσατο (13.191) | "not anywhere at the skin did it speed" | "did not reach his skin anywhere" | "touch", "graze"; εἴσατο is ἵεμαι "dart" of a missile, with the genitive of the goal |
| ἀσπίδος ὀμφαλόν (13.192) | "the boss of the shield" | "the boss of the shield" | "navel", "centre", "middle of the shield"; ὀμφαλός is the raised central knob |
| νεκρῶν ἀμφοτέρων (13.194) | "both the corpses" | "both the corpses" | "dead men", "bodies" |
| ἀρχοὶ Ἀθηναίων (13.196) | "commanders of the Athenians" | "commanders of the Athenians" | "leaders" (reserved for ἡγεμών, ἡγήτωρ), "chiefs", "captains"; follows the table’s ἀρχός "commander" (1.311, 2.493), no departure |
| θούριδος ἀλκῆς with μεμαότε (13.197) | "eager for impetuous might" | "eager for impetuous might" | "eager with" (the table’s μεμαότες ἐγχείῃσι takes the dative; here the genitive of desire); θούριδος ἀλκῆς keeps the table’s "impetuous might" |
| καρχαροδόντων (κυνῶν, 13.198) | "sharp-toothed" | "sharp-toothed" | reused from the table (10.360, καρχαρόδοντε κύνε), no departure |
| ῥωπήϊα πυκνά (13.199) | "thick brushwood" | "thick brushwood" | "thickets", "dense scrub" |
| κορυστά (Αἴαντε, dual of κορυστής, 13.201) | "helmeted" | "helmeted" | "armed", "in full armour"; from κόρυς "helmet" |
| σφαιρηδόν (13.204) | "ball-fashion" | "like a ball" | "spinning", "bowled"; σφαῖρα "ball" + -δόν |
| Ποσειδάων ἐχολώθη (13.206) | "Poseidon was angered" | "Poseidon was … angered" | "furious", "enraged"; χολόομαι "be angered", χόλος "anger" (the table), not "incensed" (χώομαι) |
| υἱωνοῖο (13.207) | "grandson" | "grandson" | "nephew", "descendant" |
| δουρικλυτὸς Ἰδομενεύς (13.210) | "Idomeneus, famed-for-the-spear" | "Idomeneus, famed for his spear" | reused from the table (5.45, 15.544), no departure |
| κατ’ ἰγνύην (13.212) | "behind the knee" | "in the hollow of the knee" | "in the leg", "in the thigh"; ἰγνύη is the back of the knee |
| κρείων ἐνοσίχθων (Poseidon unnamed, 13.215) | "the lord earth-shaker" | "the lord earth-shaker" | "wide-ruling" (εὐρὺ κρείων); κρείων keeps the table’s "lord" and ἐνοσίχθων "earth-shaker" |
| τὸν δὲ προσέφη κρείων ἐνοσίχθων (13.215) | "And him addressed the lord earth-shaker," | "The lord earth-shaker then spoke to him," | "answered", "said to"; προσέφη "addressed" in `l` as in the table’s προσέφη κρείων Ἀγαμέμνων |
| εἰσάμενος φθογγὴν … υἷϊ Θόαντι (13.216) | "making himself like in voice the son of Andraemon, Thoas" | "taking the likeness of Thoas, son of Andraemon, in voice" | "disguised as", "in the guise of"; follows the table’s εἴσατο φθογγήν (2.791) and εἰσάμενος Κάλχαντι (13.45) |
| Ἰδομενεῦ Κρητῶν βουληφόρε (13.219, 13.255) | "counsel-bearer of the Cretans" | "counsellor of the Cretans" | "adviser", "leader"; follows the table’s βουληφόρε (5.180) |
| ὄκνῳ εἴκων (13.224) | "yielding to hesitation" | "give way to hesitation" | "shrinking", "reluctance", "cowardice" |
| ἀνδύεται πόλεμον κακόν (13.225) | "shrinks back from the evil war" | "shrinks back from the evil war" | "flees", "avoids"; πόλεμον κακόν keeps the table’s "evil" |
| ὑπερμενέϊ Κρονίωνι (13.226) | "the exceeding-strong son of Cronus" | "the son of Cronus, of surpassing strength" | reused from the table (7.480–481), no departure |
| μενεδήϊος (13.228) | "foe-withstanding" | "one to stand firm against the enemy" | "steadfast", "stout", "firm in battle"; reused from the shipped 12.247 (iliad-074), no departure; μένω "stand firm" + δήϊος "hostile" |
| κυνῶν μέλπηθρα (13.233) | "playthings of dogs" | "the playthings of dogs" (+ note: sense of the noun inferred from μέλπω) | "sport for dogs", "dogs’ meat", "carrion for dogs" |
| μεθίῃσι μάχεσθαι (13.234) | "slackens in fighting" | "slackens in the fighting" | "shirks", "holds back from", "is slack to"; keeps the table’s μεθίημι "slacken" |
| συμφερτὴ ἀρετή (13.237) | "combined excellence" | "is a joint thing" (+ note on the sense) | "strength in numbers", "worth pooled", "valour"; ἀρετή keeps the table’s "excellence" |
| λυγρῶν (ἀνδρῶν, 13.237) | "grievous" | "sorry" | "wretched" (reserved for δύστηνος); `l` keeps the table’s "grievous" for λυγρός and `i` gives the sense of a man, as in the table’s λυγρὸς ἐών (13.119); "weak", "poor" |
| νῶϊ δὲ καί κ’ ἀγαθοῖσιν ἐπισταίμεσθα μάχεσθαι (13.238) | "we two would know how to fight even against good men" | same | "brave men" (the table keeps ἀγαθός "good"), "hold our own", "stand up to" |
| ὣς εἰπὼν ὃ μὲν αὖτις ἔβη θεὸς ἂμ πόνον ἀνδρῶν (13.239) | "So having spoken, he, the god, went back again into the toil of men" | "So he spoke, and the god went back again into the toil of men" | "the labour of men", "the work of war"; πόνος "toil" |
| κλισίην εὔτυκτον (13.240) | "well-made hut" | "well-made hut" | reused from the table (10.566), no departure |
| δύσετο τεύχεα καλά (13.241) | "put on his fine armour" | "put on his fine armour" | "armed himself", "donned"; δύω "put on" |
| γέντο δὲ δοῦρε (13.241) | "took two spears" | "took two spears" | follows the table’s δοῦρε "two spears" (22.125) |
| βῆ δ’ ἴμεν ἀστεροπῇ ἐναλίγκιος (13.242) | "set out to go, like lightning" | "set out like the lightning" | "went on his way" (turned down by the table), "like a flash of lightning", "like a thunderbolt"; βῆ δ’ ἴμεν "set out to go" / "set out" as in the table (5.167); ἀστεροπή "lightning" |
| ἀπ’ αἰγλήεντος Ὀλύμπου (13.243) | "from light-filled Olympus" | "from light-filled Olympus" | reused from the table (αἰγλήεις, 20.103) |
| ἀρίζηλοι δέ οἱ αὐγαί (13.244) | "conspicuous is its glare" | "its glare is conspicuous" | "gleams", "rays" (kept for αὐγή of the sun), "bright", "plain to see"; αὐγή keeps the table’s "glare" (2.456), plural in the Greek and collective in English; ἀρίζηλος keeps "conspicuous" |
| Μηριόνης … θεράπων ἐῢς (13.246) | "his good attendant" | "his good attendant" | "squire", "servant", "comrade"; θεράπων keeps the table’s "attendant" |
| σθένος Ἰδομενῆος (13.248) | "the strength of Idomeneus" | "the strength of Idomeneus" (+ note: a periphrasis for the man) | "mighty Idomeneus", "the might of" (ἴφθιμος is kept for "mighty"); σθένος keeps the table’s "strength" |
| Μηριόνη Μόλου υἱὲ πόδας ταχὺ φίλταθ’ ἑταίρων (13.249) | "Meriones, son of Molus, swift in feet, dearest of companions" | "Meriones, son of Molus, swift of foot, dearest of companions" | "swift-footed" (ποδώκης); πόδας ταχύς takes the pattern of the table’s πόδας ὠκύς, with ταχύς and ὠκύς both "swift" |
| τίπτ’ ἦλθες πόλεμόν τε λιπὼν καὶ δηϊοτῆτα; (13.250) | "why have you come, leaving war and fighting?" | same | "battle"; πόλεμον … δηϊοτῆτα keeps the table’s pair "war and fighting" |
| βέλεος … τείρει ἀκωκή (13.251) | "the point of a missile wears you down" | "does the point of a missile wear you down" | "arrow-head", "wound"; τείρω "wear down" |
| Κρητῶν … χαλκοχιτώνων (13.255) | "of the bronze-shirted Cretans" | "of the bronze-shirted Cretans" | "bronze-clad", "bronze-armoured"; χαλκοχιτών keeps the table’s "bronze-shirted" |
| κατεάξαμεν (13.257, 1 pl. for 1 sg.) | "we broke" | "I have broken" (+ note: plural ending) | "we have broken" in `i` |
| ὑπερηνορέοντος (Δηϊφόβοιο, 13.258) | "over-bold" | "overbearing" | reused from the table (ὑπερηνορεόντων, 4.176, and 6.5), no departure |
| καὶ ἓν καὶ εἴκοσι δήεις (13.260) | "even one and twenty you will find" | "you will find as many as twenty-one" | "twenty and one", "a score and one" |
| Τρώϊα (δούρατα, 13.262) | "Trojan ones" | "Trojan ones" (+ note: neuter plural agrees with the spears) | "Trojan arms"; the spears, since the next clause says they are taken from the dead |
| κταμένων ἀποαίνυμαι (13.262) | "from the slain I take away" | "I take from the slain" | "strip", "plunder"; the middle of ἀποαίνυμαι is "take for oneself" |
| ἑκὰς ἱστάμενος πολεμίζειν (13.263) | "to fight standing far from ill-disposed men" | "of fighting standing far from ill-disposed men" | "hostile" (reserved for ἀνάρσιος; δυσμενής is "ill-disposed" in the table), "from afar", "at a distance from the foe"; ὀΐω with the infinitive is "I think of" |
| ἀσπίδες ὀμφαλόεσσαι (13.264) | "bossed shields" | "bossed shields" | "shields with bosses", "round", "bucklers", "studded"; reused from the table (4.448), no departure |
| λαμπρὸν γανόωντες (13.265) | "brightly gleaming" | "gleaming brightly" | "shining", "glittering"; γανάω keeps the table’s "gleaming" (ἐπηετανὸν γανόωσαι) |
| τώ μοι δούρατά τ’ ἔστι (13.264) | "therefore I have spears" | "so I have spears" | τώ here is "therefore" (= τῷ), unlike the dual of the table’s τώ μοι μία γείνατο μήτηρ (3.238) |
| ἔτι γὰρ πολέμοιο μενοίνα ἀντιάαν (13.214–215) | "for still of war he was eager to meet it" | "for he was still eager to face the war" | "to join the fight"; μενοινάω is "be eager" (the table’s "be minded" for the subjunctive in 10.101), ἀντιάω "meet, face" |
